steps.title: What is changing here?
steps.body: The water over the reef, measured from space by NASA's MUR sea temperature record. Pick a layer on the left to see where it warmed.

steps.title: Is it real, or is it chance?
steps.body: The warming is steady and shows up across most of the sea in this map. It is not one hot summer.

steps.title: Is it the climate?
steps.body: Sea temperature is part of the climate itself, so there is nothing to split off. What changed is how often the heat piles up: heat-stress years used to be rare here, and now they keep coming back.

narrative: Coral reefs are often called the rainforests of the sea. This one sits in water that keeps getting warmer, and the hot spells that stress corals no longer wait a decade between visits.
caveats: Chlorophyll near the coast is read from water colour, which mud, river water and a shallow sea floor also change. No trend was detected.
We do not say what drives the heat stress, or whether floods change the water near the coast: this case does not test them.
